A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FlashAdventure, CUA-as-a-Judge and COAST. All 31 pages of each version, including Appendices A–C, are readable, and their text, equations, figures and tables support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GUI-agent evaluations on 34 games, human gameplay results, judge validation, ablations and supplementary experiments, including three-trial results in Appendix B.2.1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original agent evaluations, human results, judge validation, ablations and supplementary experiments.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 revises the documented solver procedure: v1 takes one action per goal with a shared nsolve cap, whereas v2 introduces an Nsolve loop for each goal. Step-limit checks move before actions. The Seek-Map-Solve architecture remains intact; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation used for the reported results changed.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 34 games across five subgenres, with identical human-study coverage and supplementary test scenarios. The text-adventure benchmarks newly discussed in Appendix A.1 are not evaluated.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparator sets remain identical, including OpenAI CUA, Claude Computer-Use, UI-TARS, Cradle and Agent S2 configurations, human baselines, prompt controls and the supplementary o4-mini comparison.

E3.justification: The experimental sections retain the 1,000-action cap, model configurations, numerical hyperparameter values, evaluation metrics, human and judge sampling, and supplementary-experiment protocols. No revised experimental execution is reported alongside the Algorithm 1 revision.

E4.justification: The component ablations, failure analysis, human diversity and observation-behavior-gap analyses, prompt control, contamination checks, hint injection and o4-mini experiments are retained unchanged. Appendix reflow does not add or remove analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report single-run main experiments and the same three-trial supplementary evaluation with means and standard deviations in Table 15. Human-gap variability reporting is also unchanged; no new seed information or statistical procedures appear.

E6.justification: Matched empirical tables and findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains COAST's 5.88% success rate and 19.89% milestone completion, while judge accuracy remains 94.00%. Per-game, ablation, multi-run and contamination results are identical.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation and reward and milestone definitions remain unchanged. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs; Algorithm 1's revision concerns procedural control flow.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims: full-story evaluation through FlashAdventure, automatic milestone judging, COAST's memory-based benefits, and the persistent agent–human performance gap.

C2.justification: Interpretations of planning, perception, lateral thinking and resource-management failures are unchanged. Both retain the same limitations concerning manual milestones, genre applicability, memory scalability and proprietary-API costs.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 retains identical model/API identifiers, hardware, runtime, trajectory context, hyperparameter values and detailed prompts. Project and game-access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix A.1 discusses TextWorld, ScienceWorld, Jericho and Jiminy Cricket, adding four references. It positions FlashAdventure as connecting text-adventure research with multimodal GUI gameplay, while retaining the existing GUI and video-game positioning.

P1.justification: v2 inserts the related-work subsection, renumbers the former Appendix A.1–A.6 as A.2–A.7, and updates cross-references. Small wording corrections occur in Section 3.5 and Table 17; the main narrative remains largely unchanged.

P2.justification: Algorithm 1 is reformatted, Table 17 is narrowed and reflowed, and existing appendix displays shift, including Figure 10 and Table 12. All 11 figures and 18 tables are retained without new visualizations.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves methodological clarity through the explicit per-goal solver loop and adds useful research context through Appendix A.1. Table 17 also fits the text width better. The empirical evidence and limitations remain unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish whether the pseudocode revision affected the implementation behind the results.
